extra.message: installAuthJdbc() concatenates the persisted data-permission rule value (getSqlRuleValue(ruleMap.get(c).getRuleValue())) directly into the permission SQL fragment, and that fragment is inserted verbatim into the MyBatis query via JeecgDemoMapper.xml:12 (`select * from demo where 1=1 ${permissionSql}`). Unlike the MyBatis-Plus sibling installAuthMplus() (line 1027, which runs SqlInjectionUtil.filterContent), no SQL-injection validation is performed here. A user who can create/edit a USE_SQL_RULES data rule (sys_permission_data_rule.rule_value) can store arbitrary SQL that is executed for every subject to that rule (stored SQL injection). Reachable via GET /test/jeecgDemo/sqlList -> JeecgDemoServiceImpl.queryListWithPermission.

SSRF: for a relative originUrl the server builds the forwarding target from CommonUtils.getBaseUrl(request)(client-controlled X_GATEWAY_BASE_PATH header or Host) and only calls CommonUtils.checkInternalUrl(baseUrl). checkInternalUrl explicitly ALLOWS loopback and link-local addresses (isLinkLocalAddress), including the cloud metadata endpoint 169.254.169.254. The resulting url is fetched server-side by restTemplate.exchange() at line 261 with the caller's admin X-Access-Token attached, so an API consumer can read cloud metadata / reach localhost services. The full-URL branch (line 321-323) applies both checkSsrfHttpUrl and checkInternalUrl; the relative branch is missing checkSsrfHttpUrl.

SSRF: when an AI plugin (flow/memory) has an empty endpoint, the tool base URL is taken from CommonUtils.getBaseUrl(currentHttpRequest), which trusts the client-supplied X_GATEWAY_BASE_PATH header (only scheme/no-userinfo/host-nonempty are checked, no internal/host allow-list). buildToolExecutor() later issues the request to baseUrl+path via RestUtil.request() (line 261). The /airag/chat/send entry point is @IgnoreAuth, and applyAuthConfig() injects the current user's X-Access-Token into the request, so an attacker can make the server call an arbitrary host and exfiltrate the bearer token.

Reflected XSS: the path variable {source} of GET /sys/thirdLogin/render/{source} is written verbatim into an HTML response (content-type text/html) with no encoding. The entire /sys/thirdLogin/** path is Shiro 'anon' (ShiroConfig.java:112), so an unauthenticated request such as /sys/thirdLogin/render/ reflects attacker script.

extra.message: Stored XSS: announcement content (data.msgContent) is interpolated into a JavaScript template literal and then assigned to contentContainer.innerHTML. The template is a plain .ftl with no FreeMarker auto-escaping and the stored value is only filtered by XssUtils.richTextXss(), which does not strip backticks or ${}, so content such as a backtick can break out of the JS literal and execute. /sys/annountCement/show/** is Shiro 'anon' (ShiroConfig.java:141), and msgContent is stored from user comments (SysCommentController /addText) and announcements.

extra.message: Missing function-level authorization / privilege escalation: SysDepartPermissionController (/sys/sysDepartPermission) has no @RequiresPermissions on any endpoint (add line 94, edit line 107, delete line 120, datarule line 205, saveDeptRolePermission line 252). The path is only protected by the JWT filter (any authenticated user). POST /sys/sysDepartPermission/saveDeptRolePermission lets any low-privileged authenticated user grant arbitrary menu permissions to a department role, and /add|/edit|/delete manipulate department permission rows.

Missing authorization + sensitive data exposure: SystemApiController (/sys/api) has no @RequiresPermissions anywhere, so any authenticated user can call GET /sys/api/getDynamicDbSourceById or /getDynamicDbSourceByCode. These return DynamicDataSourceModel, which serializes dbUrl, dbUsername and dbPassword in plaintext (DynamicDataSourceModel.java:42/52/56), disclosing database credentials. The same controller exposes queryAllUser/queryUserBySuperQuery/getUserPermissionSet (user enumeration).

Missing function-level authorization: SysPositionController (/sys/position) has no @RequiresPermissions on any endpoint (add line 111, edit line 137, delete line 162, deleteBatch line 183, savePositionUser line 386). Any authenticated user (JWT only) can create/modify/delete positions and reassign users to positions; edit() also passes the full request body to updateById (mass assignment).

Command injection: the @XxlJob("commandJobHandler") handler executes the raw job parameter as an OS command via Runtime.getRuntime().exec(command) with no validation or shell escaping. A caller able to define/trigger the job (or influence its param) obtains arbitrary OS command execution. The companion httpJobHandler (line 154) opens an arbitrary URL with no SSRF filtering.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: Disabled TLS certificate validation: createHttpClientWithNoSsl() installs an X509TrustManager whose checkClientTrusted/checkServerTrusted are empty and returns null accepted issuers, then initializes SSLContext with it. Any TLS connection made by this HttpClient (CAS login validation, reachable from the anon endpoint /sys/cas/client/validateLogin) is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle.

Weak password hashing: user passwords are derived with the PBEWithMD5AndDES algorithm using a hardcoded static salt (SALT = "63293188", line 32) and only 1000 iterations. MD5/DES is broken and fast to brute-force; a shared static salt enables precomputed/rainbow-table and cross-user attacks.
